title: O Christ, Who Art Ascended Now
description: O Christ, Who Art Ascended Now in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Latin hymns of the early Church for Hymns of the Early Church (London, 1896), headed “Alleluia!”.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Christ, who art as-cend-ed now To realms of bliss a-bove, In-spire our souls to rise to Thee, Up-borne by faith and love.

lines: O Christ, who art ascended now
To realms of bliss above,
Inspire our souls to rise to Thee,
Upborne by faith and love.
Make us to seek those holy joys,
That they who love receive;
That earthly mind can never know,
Nor faithless soul perceive.
There, where Thou art, they reap reward
Who toiled at duty’s call;
For Thou dost give Thyself to them,
And Thou art all in all.
By power divine, O let us come
Where glory cannot fade;
And from Thy heavenly throne send down
The Spirit to our aid.
To Thee who art at God’s right hand,
O Christ, to Thee be praise,
To Father, and to Holy Ghost,
Be glory given always.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns of the Early Church (1896)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Latin, public domain, as printed in Hymns of the Early Church; set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
